purpose: Bounded inventory of BBC News/BBC Sport original pages relevant to post-2-February-2023 Greenwood coverage and the later Tottenham/De Zerbi controversy. Supplementary evidence; not a BBC corpus census, prominence measure, output-volume denominator, or verdict on proportionality.

requestedAnchors: selected later transfer/football reports through 14 October 2026
scope.sourceRule: Only BBC original pages directly opened and visibly inspected are marked publisher_verified. One BBC AV page and one live-report page are separately identified to prevent double counting. Search snippets, URL dates and derived link text are not treated as publication-date verification.

legalContext.summary: The CPS discontinued the proceedings on 2 February 2023 before trial. BBC reports describe the CPS reason as withdrawal of key witnesses and new material, leaving no realistic prospect of conviction. This was not a trial, acquittal or not-guilty verdict. The inventory records only whether each article itself mentions charges being dropped, CPS reasoning, Greenwood’s denial, or Manchester United’s internal conclusion.

countingGuide.eventCountCaveat: The page count is not the event count. Multiple distinct pages can cover the same underlying event (e.g. 2 April 2026 interview/apology); AV derivatives and liveblog posts must not be inflated into standalone articles. Some pages are transfer gossip/audience formats rather than independently reported Greenwood coverage.

assessment: This verified sample establishes that BBC attention did continue well beyond 2 February 2023, through recurring, identifiable new hooks in 2023 and 2024 and a later 2026 Tottenham appointment controversy. It also shows that some stories merely recapped the dropped charges, while others explained the CPS test/reason; the 2 April 2026 report does the latter. A bounded publisher-page sample cannot establish that coverage lasted “too long,” compare proportionality against other cases or all football transfers, or resolve a racial-bias hypothesis. The only direct race-related framing evidence found here is attributed supporter-group commentary in the 28 March 2026 BBC report; do not infer identity from appearance or turn the source’s claim into a finding.

verifiedPrimarySources.title: Ched Evans: Sheffield United will not let convicted rapist train
verifiedPrimarySources.verification: Original BBC Sport page opened; it described Evans as convicted at that time and reported the club reversing a training-facility offer after public criticism.

verifiedPrimarySources.title: Editorial Standards Committee bulletin, November and December 2016, issued February 2017
verifiedPrimarySources.verification: Official BBC Trust PDF opened. Its discussion of the 14 October 2016 BBC News Channel Ched Evans report says the bulletin opened by stating he had been found not guilty following retrial; it records the conviction-date error in the intro and says the item as a whole made clear the acquittal and why. The Trust found no evidence likely to establish an impartiality breach and did not admit the appeal.

boundedComparison.scopeDifference: This is only a legal-status/editorial-handling comparison, not a BBC article-volume comparison. Evans had an earlier conviction later quashed and was acquitted at retrial; Greenwood’s CPS case was discontinued before trial and produced no verdict. The 2014 BBC report predates Evans’s retrial and should not be compared as if published after the acquittal. Neither item establishes race, racial motivation, or a causal link between identity and BBC coverage.
